headline: Models simulate tumor evolution, persister resistance, and preclinical trial design
label: In Silico Tumor Dynamics Modeling
summary: Quantitative simulations now test combination therapy, resistance dynamics, and preclinical trial evaluation in silico.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of quantitative dynamical models to reason about intervention outcomes in tumor and leukaemia systems. The renal cell carcinoma preprint couples an ODE and stochastic cancer-immunity cycle model to pharmacokinetics to simulate advanced RCC evolution and optimize bevacizumab plus atezolizumab combination therapy. The agent-based study couples tumor population dynamics with epigenetic state inheritance during the cell cycle to simulate drug-tolerant persister-induced resistance in solid tumors. The leukaemia preprint is methodologically distinct: it compares exponential and logistic growth models fitted to mouse time series against a two-timepoint test for detecting simulated knockout effects, addressing preclinical trial evaluation rather than tissue mechanism. What is new across the set is explicit in silico testing of interventions and experimental designs.
